name: vnc
summary: Remote desktop access capability for GUI-driven tools and host-session automation workflows.
why_it_matters: VNC remains useful capability knowledge for remotely operating GUI software, but there is no current validated scenario that justifies maintaining it as an active standalone resource.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs remote access to a GUI-only tool.
Operators want browser or client access to a hosted desktop session.
The workflow depends on seeing and controlling a desktop rather than only API automation.

platform_support.notes: Remote desktop components exist across platforms, but session management, security, and display-server behavior differ materially by host.

prerequisites: Clear reason to use VNC instead of a more constrained remote UI
implementation_notes: Promotion should validate one concrete remote-desktop workflow.
Keep session hosting separate from the applications accessed through it.
Security and exposure boundaries should be explicit from the start.
operational_notes: Remote-desktop security matters more than startup convenience.
Validation should prove login and usable session control.
Host display and permission differences shape support quality.
risks: Remote desktop services expand the attack surface quickly.
A generic wrapper can imply stronger security defaults than exist.
